bull.b: Consistent and rising free cash flow from subscription operations provides durable internal funding for product R&D, M&A integration, and go-to-market investment. Strong FCF improves optionality versus reliance on external capital and supports multiyear platform expansion and margin improvement.

bull.t: High Gross Margins and Scalable Economics
bull.b: Sustained high gross margins reflect cloud-native delivery and favorable unit economics, enabling incremental ARR to flow to operating leverage. Durable margin structure underpins profitability potential as sales and G&A scale more slowly than subscription revenue, supporting long-term margin sustainability.

bull.t: Recurring Revenue Scale and ARR Momentum
bull.b: Large, growing ARR and concentrated enterprise traction create durable revenue visibility and renewal-driven cash conversion. Strong enterprise deal flow and cross-sell of ZIA/ZPA increase stickiness and average contract value, supporting multi-period revenue stability and predictable growth.

bear.b: Despite revenue and margin progress, persistent GAAP losses and negative ROE indicate the business has not yet converted scale into consistent accounting profitability. This constrains long-term capital returns and means execution must sustain margin gains to fully realize durable operating profits.

A material step-down in growth rate reduces multi-year revenue runway and raises the bar for sustaining operating leverage. Slower organic net new ARR growth pressures future margin expansion, investment prioritization, and could lengthen the timeline to consistent GAAP profitability.

bear.t: Rising CapEx and Supply-Chain Cost Pressure
bear.b: Elevated and potentially rising capex driven by AI/data center demand creates a structural headwind to free cash flow margins and raises ongoing infrastructure costs. Persistent supply-driven price pressure can compress long-term cash conversion and complicate planning for durable margin improvement.
